format:
  html:

masonry:
  item-selector: ".grid-item"
  gutter: 0
include-in-header:
  - text: |
      <style>
        .grid-item {
          width: 160px;
          height: 120px;
          float: left;
          background: #D26;
          border: 2px solid #333;
          border-color: hsla(0, 0%, 0%, 0.5);
          border-radius: 5px;
        }
        .grid-item--width2 { width: 320px; }
        .grid-item--width3 { width: 480px; }
        .grid-item--width4 { width: 640px; }

        .grid-item--height2 { height: 200px; }
        .grid-item--height3 { height: 260px; }
        .grid-item--height4 { height: 360px; }
      </style>
---

A fenced div with the `.grid` class becomes a Masonry grid, and its `.grid-item` children are laid out.
The library is loaded and initialised for you.

```markdown
:::: {.grid masonry-gutter="10"}
::: {.grid-item}
:::
::: {.grid-item .grid-item--height2}
:::
::: {.grid-item .grid-item--width2}
:::
::::
```

:::: {.grid masonry-gutter="10"}
::: {.grid-item}
:::
::: {.grid-item .grid-item--height2}
:::
::: {.grid-item}
:::
::: {.grid-item .grid-item--width2}
:::
::: {.grid-item .grid-item--height3}
:::
::: {.grid-item}
:::
::::

Masonry positions items but does not size them: the widths and heights above come from the stylesheet in this document's front matter.

Set defaults for every grid under a top-level `masonry` key, and override them per grid with `masonry-*` attributes.

Full documentation: <https://m.canouil.dev/quarto-masonry/>.
